# Chen–Kou–Lyu 2026, Lemmas 6.8–6.10 (digest)

Source: arXiv:2608.03073v2. Not a substitute for the paper.

## Definition 2.1 (finite separation)

A Scott-continuous `f : D → D` is finitely separated from the identity if
there is a finite `M ⊆ D` such that for every `x`, some `m ∈ M` satisfies
`f(x) ≤ m ≤ x`.

## Lemma 6.8

If `f` is Scott-continuous and finitely separated from `id`, then
`f(x) ≪ x` for every `x`.

## Lemma 6.3 / 6.9 (2-level flattening)

Let `(a_i)` be increasing, `a_i ≤ id`, `⊔ a_i = id`. For each `i` let
`(h_{i,j})` be increasing, `h_{i,j} ≤ id`, `⊔_j h_{i,j} = a_i`, each
`h_{i,j}` finitely separated. Then `S = {h_{i,j}²}` is directed, has
supremum `id`, and contains an increasing cofinal sequence. Squares
remain finitely separated and factor through the same intermediate object.

## Theorem 6.10(ii)

If `D` is a domain, `a_n = e_n p_n ≤ id`, `⊔ a_n = id`, and each
intermediate `B_n` is in `ωFVA`, then `D ∈ ωFVA`.
